title: Intel CEO says he uses AI agents every day to cut hours of research to minutes
gist: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says he uses AI agents (including Claude) daily, turning two days of research into five minutes, frames the shift from foundation models to inference to agentic AI, and calls AI bigger than the internet; Intel shares rose 37.5% in a month to a $650B market value on agent-driven compute demand hopes.

insights.claim: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says he uses many AI agents every day for research and speech preparation, cutting the time to understand an unfamiliar subject from two days to five minutes.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: CEO-level daily usage is an adoption signal supporting agent-driven inference demand.
insights.quote: instead of spending two days, I can use the agents to understand in five minutes

insights.claim: Lip-Bu Tan says he uses Anthropic's Claude to learn about quantum computing and other emerging technologies.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Shows frontier LLM products penetrating executive knowledge work.
insights.quote: I use Claude to understand and explain to me.

insights.claim: Tan describes AI moving from today's foundation models toward inference and then agentic AI, where systems carry out sequences of tasks rather than respond to single prompts.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Multi-step agents imply far more compute per user task, supporting CPU and accelerator demand.

insights.claim: Tan believes AI will ultimately be bigger than the internet.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Signals Intel leadership's strategic commitment to AI-oriented positioning.
insights.locator: Tan has been an AI investor

insights.claim: Intel shares rose 37.5% over the past month, taking its market value to $650 billion, near its June rally levels, coinciding with renewed investor interest in AI agents creating demand for more computing capacity.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The market is pricing Intel as an agentic-AI compute beneficiary, raising expectation risk.
insights.quote: Intel shares have risen 37.5% over the past month, pushing the company's market value to $650 billion

insights.claim: Tan invests his own money in technologies too early or uncertain for his venture fund, moving to fund investments only once a clear commercial application emerges.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A staged personal-then-fund approach illustrates how seasoned VCs de-risk frontier tech bets.

insights.claim: Tan's AI investments have spanned semiconductor companies, AI software, frontier models and predictive applications since before the current boom.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Context for potential conflicts and conviction in Intel's AI strategy.
insights.locator: Tan has been an AI investor
